text: "Precious in the sight of the Lord is the death of His saints." Precious here means costly: losing you early costs Him.
explanation:
This verse is often read as though God treasures His people dying. But the Hebrew word means costly, like an expensive jewel. And look at the context: "For You have delivered my soul from death, my eyes from tears, and my feet from falling." The psalmist was celebrating that God kept him alive.

When a believer goes home before their time, all the gifts, anointing and wisdom God has poured into them leave this earth with them. You can't lead someone to Jesus or pass on what you've learned once you're in heaven. Paul knew it: "To remain in the flesh is more needful for you." Your life here matters to Him.

text: Wisdom has two hands: long life in her right hand, riches and honour in her left. Solomon received only the left.
explanation:
"Length of days is in her right hand, in her left hand riches and honour." Solomon asked for wisdom and became fabulously wealthy and honoured, but he didn't live a particularly long life. He missed wisdom's right hand.

One thing Solomon lacked was what Job longed for: a mediator between God and man. You have one. Jesus, God's wisdom in person, lives at the Father's right hand "to make intercession" for you. When you embrace Him, you're embraced by both of wisdom's hands.

text: At 85, Caleb said, "I'm as strong as ever." At 80, Barzillai said, "I can't taste or hear; I'd be a burden." Same era, different confessions.
explanation:
Barzillai was a wealthy, generous man who had fed David's men when Absalom drove him from Jerusalem. When David returned, he urged Barzillai, "Cross over with me, and I will provide for you in Jerusalem." But Barzillai answered with a list of his age's limitations and asked to go home and die near his parents' grave. He sent his son Chimham instead.

It's easy to think we're a burden when we come to our greater David. But the Lord says, "Let me see your face, let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet." He's inviting you to cross over and live where He is, so that He can provide for you there. Don't answer His invitation with excuses about your age.

text: David seems to have given Chimham a place near Bethlehem. Centuries later, in Bethlehem, there was "no room in the inn."
explanation:
Barzillai's son Chimham went to Jerusalem with David. Centuries later Jeremiah mentions "the habitation of Chimham, which is near Bethlehem," a lodging place for travellers. It's possible that David gave Chimham his own family home in Bethlehem, passed down from Boaz and Ruth through Obed and Jesse, and it became an inn.

If so, picture the night a young couple arrived in Bethlehem, Mary about to give birth. The child she carried was the true heir to everything David owned. Yet the rightful owner was turned away from His own family home: "there was no room for them in the inn."

text: Jonathan loved David, but stayed in Saul's palace. Love Jesus all the way, not from a distance.
explanation:
Jonathan loved David as his own soul and made a covenant with him. Yet when David was rejected and hunted, the men who shared his caves were the ones who reigned with him later, among them Gentiles like Ittai. Jonathan stayed in his father's palace, and he died with Saul on Mount Gilboa, in the wrong place at the wrong time.

Jesus told His disciples, "You are those who have continued with Me in My trials. And I bestow upon you a kingdom." Some believers are content simply to be saved and love Jesus from the safety of the palace. Go all the way with Him. That's where the richest blessings are.

text: If your healing is coming slowly, thirty, then sixty, then a hundredfold, God may be preparing a testimony through you.
explanation:
Under the law, sacrificial lambs were killed quickly; none were tortured first. But Jesus was scourged before He was crucified, because "by His stripes we are healed." Healing is yours, and every time you take communion you can discern His body broken for your health.

Some receive their healing instantly. For others it unfolds gradually: thirtyfold, then sixtyfold, then a hundredfold. Don't be discouraged if yours is slow; it may seem worse before it gets better. God may be making you a trophy of His grace, someone who will later encourage many still waiting for their own manifestation.

text: Even while Joseph was a slave, "the Lord was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man."
explanation:
Joseph had been sold by his brothers and owned nothing, not even himself. Yet Scripture calls him prosperous. The Hebrew tsalach describes a person whose whole life God makes succeed, regardless of their bank balance. It's the same word in Psalm 1: whoever meditates on God's Word is like a tree planted by rivers of water, "and whatever he does shall prosper."

That's the kind of prosperity John prayed for: "Beloved, I pray that you may prosper in all things and be in health, just as your soul prospers." Spirit, soul and body, God wants you to flourish, even in circumstances that look like slavery.
